a set of SG cells labeled by GFP in a transgenic line of mice are morphologically and electrophysiologically homogeneous and are involved in the integration/modulation of C-fiber primary sensory afferent activity.

GFP-expressing neurons in the spinal cord SG are a set of morphologically similar neurons with similar physiological properties that receive input from C-fiber afferents and are upregulated by noxious stimuli.
a set of spinal SG neurons selectively labeled with GFP have homogenous morphology, physiology, and response to noxious stimulation, and are organized in a modular manner.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the functional organization of the SG and the role that the GFP-expressing neurons play in this organization.
the functional properties of a set of spinal SG neurons that are defined by GFP expression in transgenic mice.
the functional organization of the spinal cord and the role of specific spinal neurons in the processing of pain and other sensory information.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the GFP-labeled SG neurons are a subset of neurons that are part of the nociceptive circuitry of the SG.
the GFP-labeled neurons represent one of many possible functional modules in the SG.
GFP-expressing cells in the SG have the properties expected for a nociceptive interneuron.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the GFP-expressing neurons are likely involved in the processing of noxious stimuli and are organized into repeating, similar circuits in the SG.
a set of SG neuronal circuits, which may have evolved to respond to C-fiber input, are systematically distributed in the SG.
GFP-expressing neurons are an identifiable set of neurons within the SG, and they appear to be organized into functional units that may play a significant role in the processing of nociceptive input.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the GFP-labeled set of SG neurons can serve as a useful model for the study of SG circuitry.
the SG is not a homogeneous population of neurons, but rather a mosaic of functionally distinct subpopulations.
a single transgenic mouse line expressing GFP in a set of spinal SG neurons provides a powerful tool to investigate the functional properties of this important region of the pain system.
